alt: Poster: STT on F&O from 1 April 2026 - futures sale 0.05% (was 0.02%), option premium sale 0.15% (was 0.10%), option exercised 0.15% (was 0.125%); source NSE circular and Income Tax Department
text:
Since 1 April 2026, every F&O trade carries a materially higher Securities Transaction Tax, and the three rates did not move by the same amount.

Under the Finance Act, 2026, as reflected in the NSE circular on revised STT rates: futures (on sale) 0.05%, up from 0.02%. Options premium (on sale of an option) 0.15%, up from 0.10%. Sale of an option where it is exercised 0.15%, up from 0.125%. The revised rates apply to transactions executed on or after 1 April 2026.

Two details worth keeping straight: on futures and on option premium, STT is payable by the seller; on exercised options, the NSE table lists the purchaser as the payer. The Income Tax Department has clarified that, apart from F&O, STT rates remain the same.

Our reading: with a flat percentage on premium or contract value, the cost per trade now matters more for high-frequency strategies than for occasional hedgers. This is an opinion, not advice.

For practitioners: have you changed how you model per-trade costs in client or proprietary workflows since April?
